62.5% Confirmed Objective Response Rate (ORR) and 29.2% Complete Response (CR) Rate in Final Phase 2 Analysis

Median Overall Survival (OS) Not Reached at More than 4 Years of Median Follow-up

Oral Presentation at the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Congress 2026 Reinforces Ongoing TILVANCE-301 Phase 3 Trial

PHILADELPHIA and MADRID, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ: IOVA), a commercial biotechnology company focused on innovating, developing, and delivering novel polyclonal tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) therapies for patients with cancer, today announced that one-time lifileucel combined with pembrolizumab demonstrated a 62.5% ORR and a 29.2% CR rate, with median OS not reached at 50.9 months of median study follow-up in the final Phase 2 analysis in frontline advanced melanoma. The Phase 2 results were presented on October 23, 2026 in a Proffered Paper oral session at the ESMO Congress 2026 in Madrid, Spain.

In frontline advanced melanoma, approximately half of patients treated with combination immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy do not achieve long-term benefit, a widely recognized unmet need.1 Following successful adoption of lifileucel in the post-anti-PD-1 therapy setting, this Phase 2 data supports the earlier use and potential approval of lifileucel plus pembrolizumab in frontline advanced melanoma. Iovance estimates that 70,000 patients with frontline advanced melanoma are addressable each year in global markets with high prevalence.2

ESMO Presentation Highlights: Cohort 1A of the IOV-COM-202 Trial (NCT03645928)

IOV-COM-202 is a multicohort, multicenter Phase 2 trial of lifileucel plus pembrolizumab in patients with solid tumors. The final analysis in frontline advanced melanoma (Cohort 1A) included 24 patients treated with one-time lifileucel that met pre-determined manufacturing specifications and pembrolizumab monotherapy for up to 24 months.

The physician-assessed confirmed ORR by RECIST v1.1 was 62.5% (15/24; 95% CI: 40.6, 81.2), including a 29.2% CR rate. The disease control rate was 83.3% (20/24; 95% CI: 62.6, 95.3). Median duration of response (DOR) was not reached (range: 4.3 to 57.7+ months) at a median follow-up of 26.9 months for DOR.

Median progression-free survival (PFS) was 19.8 months (95% CI: 3.6 months to not reached). Median PFS after second line of therapy was 34.3 months (95% CI: 6.8 months to not reached), indicating that subsequent systemic therapy remains feasible after frontline lifileucel and pembrolizumab, including additional ICI therapy. Median OS was not reached (95% CI: 19.2 months to not reached) at a median study follow-up of 50.9 months.

Safety was consistent with the underlying disease and known safety profiles of one-time lifileucel and pembrolizumab. Late adverse events were consistent with continuous use of pembrolizumab monotherapy, further differentiating lifileucel plus pembrolizumab from ICI combinations used in the frontline setting.

“About half of patients do not experience lasting benefit with frontline combination immunotherapy for advanced melanoma,” stated Dr. Andrew J.S. Furness, Consultant Medical Oncologist and Solid Tumour Cellular Therapy Lead at The Royal Marsden National Health Service Foundation Trust, Leader of the Cellular Therapy and Translational Immunology Group at The Institute of Cancer Research, London, and Principal Investigator in IOV-COM-202 and TILVANCE-301 trials. “A single administration of lifileucel plus pembrolizumab demonstrated compelling response rates and durability that compare favorably to other ICI combination approaches in frontline advanced melanoma, with median overall survival not reached at more than four years of follow-up. These remarkable Phase 2 results provide a strong scientific rationale to investigate earlier treatment with lifileucel in the TILVANCE-301 trial.”

Translational analyses support the positive clinical results in Cohort 1A. T-cell receptor (TCR) sequencing detected clones from the infused lifileucel product in the peripheral blood for as long as 12 months after infusion (n=13), consistent with the strong DOR benefit of lifileucel.

Noah Berkowitz, M.D., Ph.D., Chief Medical Officer of Iovance, stated, “The final Cohort 1A results demonstrate unprecedented efficacy and a potentially best-in-class clinical profile for lifileucel combined with pembrolizumab in frontline advanced melanoma. These data, together with supportive translational findings, reinforce the importance of our ongoing TILVANCE-301 Phase 3 randomized trial to support a new approval for lifileucel in frontline advanced melanoma.”

The presentation is available at www.iovance.com. Iovance will also present the first clinical data for lifileucel in soft tissue sarcomas in a Rapid Oral presentation on Monday, October 26, 2026 (Abstract #3725RO).

About TILVANCE

TILVANCE-301 (NCT05727904) is a Phase 3, multicenter, open-label, randomized, parallel group, treatment study to assess the efficacy and safety of lifileucel in combination with pembrolizumab compared with pembrolizumab alone in participants with untreated, unresectable or metastatic melanoma. The trial is enrolling at more than 80 sites in the U.S., Canada, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. The dual primary endpoints are ORR and PFS assessed by independent review committee. TILVANCE-301 is designed to support approval for lifileucel in combination with pembrolizumab in frontline advanced melanoma and to serve as the confirmatory trial for full U.S. approval of Amtagvi® in previously treated advanced melanoma.

About Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc.

Iovance Biotherapeutics, Inc. is the global leader in innovating, developing, and delivering tumor infiltrating lymphocyte (TIL) cell therapies for patients with solid tumors. Amtagvi® (lifileucel) is the first FDA-approved, one-time treatment for previously treated advanced melanoma, now approved in three global markets and available at nearly 100 authorized treatment centers (ATCs). The Iovance TIL platform spans registrational trials and next-generation programs in additional solid tumors, including gene-edited and IL-12 tethered TIL therapies, next-generation IL-2, and precision immuno-oncology approaches. As the first and only company to take TIL therapy from concept to a broadly accessible commercial treatment, Iovance operates as an end-to-end cell therapy company, anchored by fully owned, centralized U.S.-based manufacturing that is scaled to serve thousands of cancer patients worldwide each year. Headquartered in Pennsylvania with offices and laboratories in California and Florida, Iovance serves patients at ATCs and clinical sites across almost the entire U.S. and in many countries around the world. About the ESMO Congress

The ESMO Congress is organized by the European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) and is one of the world’s most influential annual oncology meetings, bringing together more than 37,000 clinicians, researchers, patient advocates, and industry representatives from around the world. The ESMO Congress 2026 takes place October 23–27, 2026, at IFEMA Madrid, Spain, and features presentations of practice-changing clinical data, translational science, and educational programming across all major tumor types. (“Millar”) for $50 million, net of cash acquired and debt assumed, with additional contingent consideration payable subject to the achievement of specified financial performance targets.
